All Arguments Here

Source: R/all_args_here.R
all_args_here.Rd

Verify that all the functions used inside a function are written with all their arguments. For instance: base::paste0(letters[1:2], collapse = NULL, recycle0 = FALSE) and not paste0(letters[1:2]).

Usage

all_args_here(
  x,
  table_export = FALSE,
  fun_export = FALSE,
  out_path = ".",
  df_name = "res.tsv",
  overwrite = FALSE,
  safer_check = TRUE,
  lib_path = NULL,
  error_text = ""
)

Arguments

x

Function name, written without quotes and brackets.

table_export

Single logical value. Export the result data frame into a .tsv file? If TRUE, the data frame is not returned by the function but only exported.

fun_export

Single logical value. Export the modified function into a .R file? If TRUE, the corrected code (missing arguments added into the detected function calls, as proposed in the $STATUS column) is not returned by the function but only exported into a file made of the name of the submitted function with _safer added at the end (e.g., test_safer.R). The file contains an assignment of the modified function: test_safer <- function(...) ..., so that base::source()ing it recreates the modified function. An error is returned if the file already exists in out_path and overwrite is FALSE, and if the tested function is not designated by a function name (like test or package::test), i.e., written by an inline definition (like function(x){x}) or by a component writing (like FUN_LIST$fun). Ignored if no correction has been applied.

out_path

Single character string indicating the absolute pathway of the folder where to export the data frame or the modified function. out_path = "." (default) means the R working directory set by the user. Ignored if table_export and fun_export are FALSE.

df_name

Single character string indicating the name of the exported data frame file. Ignored if table_export is FALSE.

overwrite

Single logical value. Overwrite potential files already existing in out_path (df_name for the table export, and the function name with _safer added at the end for the fun_export)? Ignored if table_export and fun_export are FALSE.

safer_check

Single logical value. Perform the "safer" checks? If TRUE, checkings are performed before main code running (see the safer-r project): 1) correct lib_path argument value 2) required functions and related packages effectively present in local R libraries and 3) R classical operators (like "<-") not overwritten by another package because of the R scope. Warning: must be set to FALSE if this function is used inside another "safer" function to avoid pointless multiple checkings.

lib_path

Vector of characters specifying the absolute pathways of the directories containing the required packages for the function, if not in the default directories. Useful when R packages are not installed in the default directories because of lack of admin rights. More precisely, lib_path is passed through the new argument of .libPaths() so that the new library paths are c(lib_path, .libPaths()). Warning: .libPaths() is restored to the initial paths, after function execution. Ignored if NULL (default) or if the safer_check argument is FALSE: only the pathways specified by the current .libPaths() are used for package calling.

error_text

Single character string used to add information in error messages returned by the function, notably if the function is inside other functions, which is practical for debugging. Example: error_text = " INSIDE <PACKAGE_1>::<FUNCTION_1> INSIDE <PACKAGE_2>::<FUNCTION_2>.". If NULL, converted into "".

Value

A message saying whether arguments are missing or everything seems fine, and a data frame indicating the missing arguments (see the column descriptions below). If table_export argument is FALSE, the data frame is returned as a message. If TRUE, it is exported as df_name in out_path. If fun_export argument is FALSE, the modified function (an R function object rebuilt from the corrected code, with its comments and indentation preserved if the submitted function carries its source references, see the details section) is returned, or NULL (invisible) if no modification has been applied. If TRUE, the modified function is exported as <FUNCTION_NAME>_safer.R in out_path and NULL is returned (invisible), or nothing is exported if no modification has been applied. A warning and NULL (invisible) are returned if the submitted function is empty of function, or only made of comments, or only made of function, if, for, while, repeat, else. Column descriptions:

  • $LINE_NB: the line number in the function code (starting at the "<- function" line, i.e., without counting the #' header lines).

  • $FUN_NAME: the function name.

  • $FUN_ARGS: the written arguments of FUN_NAME. "NOT_CONSIDERED" means that the function is between quotes or after $.

  • $FUN_POS: the position of the first character of the function name in the $LINE_NB line.

  • $DEF_ARGS: the defaults arguments of FUN_NAME. "NO_ARGS" means that the function has no arguments. "INTERNAL_FUNCTION" means that the function has been created inside the checked function. "SKIPPED" means that the function is not analyzed for the reason indicated in the "details" section.

  • $MISSING_ARG_NAMES: the missing argument names in FUN_ARGS.

  • $MISSING_ARGS: the missing arguments with their values in FUN_ARGS.

  • $STATUS: either "GOOD", meaning that all the arguments are already written, or a new proposal of arguments writing, or indicates if some arguments are not fully written (abbreviation is discouraged), or nothing.

An additional message "EVERYTHING SEEMS CLEAN" if the $STATUS column is only made of "" and "GOOD".

An additional message "ARGUMENTS WITH EMPTY VALUE" listing, for each line and function, the arguments written (or proposed in the $STATUS column) with an empty value (like envir = ), with their default value, i.e., the potential flaws of the code (see the details section). Use "= ," or "= )" to seek each case in the code.

An additional message "CORRECTIONS NOT APPLIED" listing the proposals of the $STATUS column that have not been inserted into the modified function, each followed by a REASON: line explaining why. These calls are left unchanged in the modified function and must be corrected manually (see the details section).

Details

More precisely, all_args_here() verifies that all the strings before an opening bracket ( are written with all their arguments. Thus, it cannot check function names written without brackets, like in the FUN argument of some functions, e.g., sapply(1:3, FUN = as.character).

The Perl regex used to detect a function name is: "([a-zA-Z]|\.[a-zA-Z._])[a-zA-Z0-9._]*\s*\(".

Currently, all_args_here() cannot detect functions written between quotes, like "+"() or "rownames<-"(x, "a").

Function names preceded by $ are not considered.

The following R functions are skipped: function, if, for, while, repeat and else.

Empty argument values (see the safer-r rules): 1) a default value that cannot be copied into the call is proposed with an empty value, meaning that the default value is used but cannot be fixed. This is the case when the default value depends on another argument (e.g., envir = as.environment(pos) in utils::getFromNamespace(), proposed as utils::getFromNamespace(x, ns, pos = -1, envir = )), on a variable of the internal environment of the function, or on the frame where it is evaluated (e.g., parent.frame()), because such a default value would be evaluated in the environment of the tested function and not in the one of the called function. 2) An argument with no default value and not written is also proposed with an empty value, because absence of value can mean something (e.g., base::.libPaths(new = , include.site = TRUE) returns the paths of the R libraries, whereas base::.libPaths(new = base::.libPaths(), include.site = TRUE) sets them). In both cases, the behavior of the code is not changed. It is recommended to test (using testthat) that these default values are unchanged, for instance testthat::expect_identical(object = base::formals(fun = utils::getFromNamespace)$envir, expected = base::quote(expr = as.environment(pos))).

Most of the time, all_args_here() does not check inside comments, but some unexpected writing could dupe all_args_here(). Please, report here if it is the case.

The returned line numbers are indicative, depending on which source is checked. For instance, saferDev::report (compiled) has not the same line numbers as its source file. Notably, compiled functions do not have comments anymore, compared to the same source function sourced into the working environment. In addition, the counting starts at the "<- function" line, i.e., without counting the #' header lines potentially present in source files.

The function works first by replacing in the code: 1) the three consecutive characters '"' or '"' by three spaces, 2) "\"'" and '\'"' by four spaces and 3) escape quotes like \" or \' by two spaces.

Pre-check: the submitted function is first checked by lambda_check(): if some lambda functions are written with the \(x) shorthand, an error is returned asking to run saferDev::lambda_check() first, because the \ writings are not managed by the text-based detection of all_args_here(). As in lambda_check(), the \(x) writing is only detectable in a function carrying its source references (attribute srcref): a compiled or loaded package function prints function(x), so that the pre-check silently passes in that case.

Known limitation: a string literal containing an escaped backslash-quote, like "'\'", desynchronizes the in-quotes detection of all_args_here(), which can return an internal error (see the dev/repro_all_args_here_internal_error_3.R script of the package repository). Please, report here if it is the case.

Line breaks, comments and indentation of the modified function (fun_export argument and returned function): the $STATUS proposals are not pasted in place of the calls. Instead, the missing arguments are inserted into the printed code of the submitted function, at the positions given by the R parser: a missing argument whose value is written without its name (e.g., round(v)) gets its name inserted before this value (round(x = v, digits = 0)), and the other missing arguments are inserted after the last argument of the call. Thus, the line breaks, the indentation, the comments and the strings of the submitted function are kept, including inside calls written on several lines, and nested calls (e.g., paste0(mean(1:2))) are all corrected. The comments and the original indentation require that the submitted function carries its source references (attribute srcref, i.e., options(keep.source = TRUE) when the function was created, the default in interactive sessions). Otherwise (e.g., a function of an installed package, or a function created in an Rscript session), the printed code is the deparsed code, without comments and with a standard indentation, but its line breaks are kept.

Corrections not applied: the call is left unchanged in the modified function and its proposal is listed in the "CORRECTIONS NOT APPLIED" message, with one of the following reasons: 1) the $MISSING_ARGS or $DEF_ARGS column of the call cannot be read; 2) the call cannot be located in the code of the function (e.g., call with an empty argument, like c(1, )); 3) the corrected call does not parse as R code; 4) an argument is written positionally and is also proposed with its name (e.g., sum(x, na.rm) proposed as sum(x, na.rm, na.rm = FALSE)), which would fail at call time; 5) the corrected call does not match the $STATUS proposal (compared whatever the order of the named arguments, the spaces, the line breaks and the comments). Of note, an empty argument value in a proposal (like envir = , see above) is never a reason: such a proposal is applied.

See more examples here.

Warnings:

  1. The following R functions are also skipped (as indicated by "SKIPPED" in the DEF_ARGS column of the returned data frame): as.environment() (see the R bug report 18849 in the R bug tracker).

  2. Some functions, like rownames(), have different arguments depending on whether something is assigned to it (e.g., rownames(x) <- "a") or not. The all_args_here() function always proposes the arguments defined in the help page without assignment, meaning that it cannot detect the assignment. A way to bypass this is to use the "exact" writing of the function. For instance, base::"rownames<-"(x, "a") instead of using base::rownames(x) <- "a", and use getAnywhere("rownames<-") to see the arguments of the function.

  3. The function could not properly work if any comma is present in default argument values. Please, report here if it is the case.

  4. Proposals in the STATUS column are only suggestions, as it is difficult to anticipate all the exceptions with arguments writing.

Examples

# Warning: these examples may not work well when using the "Run examples" link 
# because of a particular environment. Please, copy-paste in a local environment.
# See also https://safer-r.github.io/saferDev/articles/all_args_here.html
fun1 <- function(x){
    base::paste0(x, "a") # collapse and recycle0 arguments not written
}
fun1_safer <- saferDev::all_args_here(x = fun1, safer_check = FALSE) # arguments added
#> 
#> INSIDE fun1(), ARGUMENTS ARE MISSING.
#> 
#>   LINE_NB FUN_NAME       FUN_ARGS FUN_POS
#> 1       3   paste0 paste0(x, "a")       7
#>                                 DEF_ARGS  MISSING_ARG_NAMES
#> 1 ..., collapse = NULL, recycle0 = FALSE collapse, recycle0
#>                        MISSING_ARGS
#> 1 collapse = NULL, recycle0 = FALSE
#>                                              STATUS
#> 1 paste0(x, "a", collapse = NULL, recycle0 = FALSE)
#> 
fun1_safer # corrected function
#> function (x) 
#> {
#>     base::paste0(x, "a", collapse = NULL, recycle0 = FALSE)
#> }
#> <environment: 0x561a7a5855d8>
# Write the table (res.tsv) and the corrected function (fun1_safer.R) in a new temporary folder:
tempo_dir <- base::tempfile(pattern = "dir", tmpdir = base::tempdir(), fileext = "")
base::dir.create(path = tempo_dir, showWarnings = TRUE, recursive = FALSE, mode = "0777")
saferDev::all_args_here(x = fun1, table_export = TRUE, fun_export = TRUE, out_path = tempo_dir,
    safer_check = FALSE)
#> 
#> INSIDE fun1(), ARGUMENTS ARE MISSING.
#> RESULT EXPORTED IN:
#> /tmp/RtmpgFv7ID/dir17921c227840/res.tsv
#> 
#> MODIFIED CODE EXPORTED IN:
#> /tmp/RtmpgFv7ID/dir17921c227840/fun1_safer.R
#>
